questions.question: The <h1> tag should be used for the ______ title of your page.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <h1> is for the main title of your page, like a book title. Each page should have only one main title.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <h1> is for the main title of your page, like a book title. Each page should have only one main title.

questions.question: For regular text blocks, use the <______> tag.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Use the <p> tag (short for 'paragraph') for regular text blocks. It's the standard way to mark up paragraphs in HTML.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Use the <p> tag (short for 'paragraph') for regular text blocks. It's the standard way to mark up paragraphs in HTML.

questions.question: There are ______ levels of headings in HTML.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: HTML provides six heading levels: <h1>, <h2>, <h3>, <h4>, <h5>, and <h6>. Each has different importance and default size.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: HTML provides six heading levels: <h1>, <h2>, <h3>, <h4>, <h5>, and <h6>. Each has different importance and default size.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <h6> creates the smallest heading. It has the lowest importance in the heading hierarchy.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <h6> creates the smallest heading. It has the lowest importance in the heading hierarchy.

questions.question:
Each paragraph should be wrapped in its own

and

______.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Paragraphs should be wrapped in <p> and </p> tags. Tags are the angle-bracket elements that define HTML elements.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Paragraphs should be wrapped in <p> and </p> tags. Tags are the angle-bracket elements that define HTML elements.

questions.question: Screen readers use heading structure to help ______ users.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Visually impaired users rely on screen readers that use heading structure to navigate pages. Proper headings make websites accessible to everyone.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Visually impaired users rely on screen readers that use heading structure to navigate pages. Proper headings make websites accessible to everyone.

questions.question: Don't skip heading ______ (e.g., from h1 to h3).

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Don't skip heading levels! Always go in order: <h1> → <h2> → <h3>, etc. Skipping levels confuses screen readers and breaks the logical structure.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Don't skip heading levels! Always go in order: <h1> → <h2> → <h3>, etc. Skipping levels confuses screen readers and breaks the logical structure.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <h2> is perfect for section titles. If <h1> is the book title, <h2> are the chapter titles within that book.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <h2> is perfect for section titles. If <h1> is the book title, <h2> are the chapter titles within that book.

questions.question: Paragraphs automatically have ______ above and below them.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Paragraphs automatically have spacing (margins) above and below them. This creates visual separation between paragraphs without extra CSS.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Paragraphs automatically have spacing (margins) above and below them. This creates visual separation between paragraphs without extra CSS.

questions.question: Proper heading structure helps ______ engines understand your content.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Proper heading structure helps search engines (like Google) understand what your page is about, which can improve your search rankings.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Proper heading structure helps search engines (like Google) understand what your page is about, which can improve your search rankings.
